newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower in thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower in thin turnover.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed softer in lighter-than-usual trading as investors awaited first-quarter corporate results and a welter of U.S. economic figures due out this week, traders said.
The cautious mood is expected to extend to Tuesday's opening, with traders watching to see how Wall Street reacts to U.S. wage data slated for release before the market opens.
The 40-share index closed down 0.06 percent at 117.04 points. The general index shed 0.15 percent to 5,313.51 points.
Volume shrank to seven billion pesos from 11 billion pesos on Friday.

Telecom CTC, which had rallied in recent weeks, slipped amid the perception that the stock had become overpriced, said Jaime Pena y Lillo, portfolio manager at Socimer. "CTC is trading at a p/e ratio of 18, which is too expensive," he said.
Other traders said the price was not justified given the lower-than-expected increase in operating earnings in the first three months of the year.
Among the other decliners, pension fund manager Provida plunged 6.96 percent to 7,801 pesos. Traders said they did not know the reason for the slide.
The gainers included winery San Pedro, which climbed amid expectations that it will report strong first-quarter earnings, said Pena y Lillo.
San Pedro shares closed 1.28 percent higher at 3.16 pesos.
